CausalChain: PCSK9 overexpression -> MHC I degradation -> Impaired antigen presentation -> Diminished CD8+ T-cell recognition -> Immune evasion; PCSK9 overexpression -> Oncogenic lipid metabolic reprogramming -> Ferroptosis resistance -> Tumor cell survival; PCSK9 inhibition -> Restoration of MHC I and metabolic vulnerability -> Enhanced antigen presentation and tumor cell sensitization; Enhanced antigen presentation + PD-1 blockade -> Synergistic anti-tumor immune response
Hypothesis: In HCC, PCSK9 overexpression promotes immune evasion via two interconnected mechanisms: it facilitates the degradation of MHC class I molecules, thereby impairing antigen presentation, and it reprograms lipid metabolism to shield tumor cells from ferroptosis. We propose that specific inhibition of PCSK9 — using modern genomic and proteomic technologies — will reverse these effects by restoring MHC class I expression and disrupting metabolic protection. The consequent enhancement in antigen presentation, when combined with PD-1 blockade that releases T-cell inhibitory checkpoints, will synergistically reactivate CD8+ T-cell responses, leading to a robust anti-tumor immune effect.
Abstract: Recent studies have illuminated that in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), PCSK9 overexpression contributes to immune evasion not only by mediating the degradation of MHC class I molecules but also by dysregulating oncogenic lipid metabolism, which may induce resistance to ferroptosis. Building upon the original concept that PCSK9 inhibition restores MHC class I expression and boosts antigen presentation, we now propose a dual-mechanistic hypothesis. By leveraging advanced techniques such as CRISPR gene editing and single-cell immune profiling, we will validate the role of PCSK9 in both MHC class I degradation and metabolic perturbations. We hypothesize that targeted inhibition of PCSK9 will restore MHC class I surface expression and dismantle metabolic adaptations that support immune evasion. When combined with PD-1 blockade, this approach is expected to synergistically enhance CD8+ T-cell mediated anti-tumor immunity and improve clinical outcomes in HCC patients.
Orignal_vs_New: The original hypothesis focused solely on PCSK9-mediated degradation of MHC class I and the subsequent immune evasion, with the expectation that PCSK9 inhibition would restore antigen presentation and synergize with PD-1 blockade. The revised hypothesis retains this central idea but enriches it by incorporating an additional metabolic dimension—recognizing that PCSK9 also modulates lipid metabolism to confer ferroptosis resistance. Moreover, contemporary technological advancements such as CRISPR gene editing and single-cell immune profiling are integrated into our approach to enhance mechanistic validation and translational potential. This comprehensive model addresses the multifactorial nature of immune evasion in HCC, reinforcing both the antigen presentation and metabolic vulnerabilities to achieve a synergistic therapeutic effect.
